_comment: Canonical prompt registry for Helmsman. Each prompt mirrors exactly what is documented in README.md. `npm run seed:prompts` pushes every entry to the Admin Service (POST /admin/prompts + variants). When the Admin Service is unreachable (demo mode / ADMIN_LOCAL_FALLBACK=true), sdk/admin-client.ts and apps/agents/app/admin_client.py read the active variant directly from this file. Variables use Mustache {{var}} syntax; the SDK render() also accepts ${var}.

prompts.description: Agent 1 — Classifier. Routes an issue into one of six categories; drives the rest of the pipeline.
prompts.model_rationale: Fast, cheap, non-thinking. Classification is a bounded single-label task — reasoning tokens add latency without accuracy here.
prompts.fallback: On malformed JSON or timeout (8s), default to {category: 'needs_info', confidence: 0.0} and flag for manual triage; the case still advances so a human always sees it.

prompts.description: Agent 2 — Context Retriever. Re-ranks the top-5 pgvector candidates by true semantic relatedness and flags likely duplicates.
prompts.model_rationale: Re-ranking 5 short candidates is a comparison task, not open-ended reasoning. qwen3-8b reads all five at once cheaply.
prompts.fallback: On malformed output, fall back to the raw cosine order from pgvector and set likely_duplicate_of=null (never auto-flag a duplicate without the model's agreement).

prompts.description: Agent 3 — Reproducer. Reads bug reports and reasons about minimal reproduction. Never executes code.
prompts.model_rationale: Code-specialized model parses snippets, stack traces and version strings far better than a general model of the same size.
prompts.fallback: On malformed output, return has_reproduction=false with all confidences 0.0 and a note that automatic analysis failed; the human still reviews.

prompts.description: Agent 4 — Source Analyzer. Loads the top-3 relevant source files (full contents) into one long-context call and forms a defect hypothesis.
prompts.model_rationale: Three full source files plus the bug description routinely exceed 32K tokens; the 262K window loads them all in one pass so the hypothesis sees cross-file context.
prompts.fallback: On malformed output or context overflow, drop to the single highest-scored file and retry once; if still failing, return likely_files from the heuristic only with confidence 0.0.

prompts.description: Agent 5 — Voice Profiler. Builds a reusable style fingerprint from a maintainer's recent comments. Thinking mode on.
prompts.model_rationale: Style abstraction across 100 samples benefits from reasoning; thinking mode lets the model weigh cadence/formatting/warmth before committing to the fingerprint.
prompts.fallback: On malformed output, write a neutral default fingerprint (tone='technical', technical_depth=3, uses_code_blocks=true) so the Responder still has something to match.
prompts.fires_at_stage: On repo connect; refreshed after each approved response (not a per-issue stage).

variants.content:
You are the Voice Profiler agent in Helmsman. You analyze how a specific maintainer writes when they respond to issues, so future drafts can match their voice. You are building a reusable style fingerprint, not summarizing content.

Maintainer: @{{maintainer_login}}
Below are up to 100 of their recent issue / PR comments, newest first, each delimited by ---:
{{comments_block}}

Measure their style empirically from these samples. Where the sample set is too small to be sure, pick the safest typical value rather than an extreme. Think step by step about cadence, formatting, warmth, and technical depth, then output the fingerprint.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object matching this exact shape:
{
  "avg_sentence_length": <number, words per sentence>,
  "uses_code_blocks": <bool>,
  "hedging_phrases": ["<phrase actually observed>"],
  "typical_opening_patterns": ["<how they tend to start, e.g. 'Thanks for the report'>"],
  "tone": "formal" | "casual" | "technical" | "warm",
  "emoji_frequency": <number, emojis per comment on average>,
  "technical_depth": 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5,
  "preferred_closing": "<how they tend to end>",
  "example_phrases": ["<short verbatim phrase that is characteristic>"]
}

prompts.description: Agent 6 — Responder. Drafts the maintainer-voiced reply from all upstream outputs. Reasoning mode.
prompts.model_rationale: The hardest generation in the pipeline: synthesize 5 upstream findings into a reply that matches a measured voice fingerprint. Reasoning mode materially improves coherence and voice fidelity.
prompts.fallback: On malformed output, fall back to a templated reply assembled from the upstream summaries (no voice match) and mark draft_quality='fallback' so the dashboard shows a degraded badge.

prompts.description: Responder self-check pass. Scores the draft against the voice fingerprint and returns a revised draft. Gated by feature flag helmsman.voice_self_check.
prompts.model_rationale: Same model as the Responder so the critique uses the same understanding of the fingerprint it just wrote against.
prompts.fallback: If self-check fails, keep the original draft and set voice_match_score=null (the dashboard then shows the pre-check estimate).
prompts.fires_at_stage: Drafting (immediately after Responder, when flag enabled)

prompts.description: Agent 7 — Prioritizer. Assigns a 1-10 triage priority via a fixed weighted rubric.
prompts.model_rationale: Rubric scoring with provided signals is structured extraction; the small non-thinking model is deterministic and fast.
prompts.fallback: On malformed output, compute the score deterministically from the same rubric in Python (the weights are fixed) so a priority always exists.
prompts.fires_at_stage: Investigation (runs in parallel with the bug-only agents)

prompts.description: Single-agent baseline for the Agent Society A/B benchmark. One qwen3-8b call does classify + label + prioritize + draft in one shot.
prompts.model_rationale: Intentionally the cheapest single call to represent the naive one-agent approach the seven-agent pipeline is measured against.
prompts.fires_at_stage: Benchmark only (not part of the production pipeline).

prompts.description: LLM-judge prompt used by the benchmark to score response quality 1-5. Run with qwen3-32b reasoning.
prompts.model_rationale: Quality judgments need reasoning; the strongest available model judges both pipelines identically to keep the A/B fair.
